solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hack pursuing dull old tax collector

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the hacking word comes after the dull one

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
to hack is to hew, chop roughly

explanation.surface: A hack journalist chasing a boring former taxman for a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist but is the verb to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Matthew was a publican, a tax gatherer, before following Jesus in the Gospel account.

clue.text: Display staff one attached to iron post

parts.note: to man is to staff
I is the Roman numeral one
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a station is a post, a place of duty

explanation.surface: A display of a stick with a single iron fitting fixed to a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifestation is an outward showing or display of something, a public demonstration.

clue.text: Unrest in essence coming after time for speaking out

indicators.note: coming after means the oil follows the spoken time word
for speaking out means the time word is said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a term is a period of time
an essence is an essential oil

explanation.surface: Discontent within a perfume essence, voiced after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of confusion and agitation, which is unrest.

clue.text: Crane with piping used to save lives

indicators.note: used to save means the hot word holds the existing word inside it

parts.note: piping hot means very hot
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A crane fitted with hoses for rescue work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a lifting device, and a crane is a machine for hoisting loads.

clue.text: Rice, as we suspect, affected sage

indicators.note: suspect suggests something doubtful or dodgy, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rice, we suspect, is putting on the airs of a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who pretends to wisdom, a know-all who affects being sage.

clue.text: Uniform, black, acceptable to employers?

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: A job interview tip: a smart black uniform will please the people hiring you.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'employers' are not bosses but anyone who employs, that is uses, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable is fit for use, so those who put it to use find it acceptable.

clue.text: Neglected aftersun? Sunglasses can reveal it

indicators.note: can reveal it means the letters sit inside the words aftersun and sunglasses

explanation.surface: Forgotten the after-sun lotion? Your sunglasses might show you have.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsung means not praised or celebrated, so overlooked and neglected.

clue.text: A year without books: one way to cause ill-feeling

indicators.note: without means outside, so A and Y go around the rest

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Spending a year with no books is one way to create resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a deep dislike or aversion, a synonym for hostility.

clue.text: What might have altered a politician such as Lloyd George?

definitions.text: What might have altered a politician such as Lloyd George?

parts.words: What might have altered a politician such as Lloyd George?
parts.note: a printer's misprint changing one letter could turn Lloyd George's party label into a different word

explanation.walkthrough: Lloyd George was a Liberal prime minister; a single wrong letter turns LIBERAL into LITERAL, and a literal is the printer's term for such a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing jargon a literal is a typographical error, a misprint of one letter for another.

clue.text: Trumpet-bearer at the front calling Russians to assemble

indicators.note: to assemble means the letters are gathered and put together in a new order
at the front picks the opening letter of the word calling

parts.note: first letter of calling

explanation.surface: A herald with a trumpet stands at the head of a crowd, summoning Russians to gather.
explanation.walkthrough: C (the front of 'calling') plus RUSSIANS are rearranged into the flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil, genus Narcissus, has a trumpet-shaped corona, so the plant literally bears a trumpet.

clue.text: Chap returning compliment finally in spades?

indicators.note: returning means the whole result is read backwards
in places the closing letter inside the card word

parts.note: spades is a suit in a deck of cards

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word compliment

parts.note: last letter of compliment

explanation.surface: A man paying back flattery generously, in spades.
explanation.walkthrough: T (end of 'compliment') goes inside SUIT giving SUTIT, which read backwards is the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is a man's name, and in crosswords any male first name can be clued as a chap.

clue.text: Exchange ending finally with malign chants?

definitions.text: Exchange ending finally with malign chants?

indicators.note: exchange means swapping the letters around into a new order
finally takes the closing letter of the word ending

parts.note: last letter of ending

explanation.surface: A row that closes with nasty chanting on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: G (end of 'ending') with MALIGN CHANTS is rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanging match is a bitter quarrel of insults traded back and forth, an exchange of abuse.

clue.text: Disdain shown by Yankee neglecting to depart from Heathrow?

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving the Yankee letter out of the flying phrase

parts.note: to fly out is to leave by plane, as from Heathrow, London's main airport
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American shows contempt by not bothering to leave from Heathrow airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' seems to be an American traveller but is just the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule is to treat it with open contempt, showing disdain for it.

clue.text: Rest vase on an article, somewhere high up

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the rest and vase follow the word an

parts.note: a nap is a short rest
an urn is a kind of vase
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A household instruction to stand a vase on some item.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapurna is a Himalayan mountain massif in Nepal, so it is a place very high up.

clue.text: Small class, without room to display little creature in fine case

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
ilk means kind or class
w/o is the written abbreviation of without
rm is the abbreviation of room, as in property listings

explanation.surface: A tiny class, with no room for it, displays a small animal in a glass case.
explanation.definitionFit: The silk moth's larva spins a cocoon of fine silk, so it lies enclosed in a delicate case.

clue.text: Land north of Italian port, just about the most bleak

indicators.note: north of in a down clue means the land word sits above the port

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it

indicators.note: just about means almost all, dropping the last letter of the port

parts.note: Trieste is a port in north-east Italy

explanation.surface: Territory above an Italian harbour that is very nearly the most dismal place.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintriest means most wintry, coldest and most cheerless, so the bleakest.

clue.text: Following urban road, a trail leads to camp

indicators.note: Following means the a and trail come after the road

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road in a town
to lag is to trail behind

explanation.surface: Directions: take the city street and a path leads you to a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for ordinary soldiers in the Second World War.

clue.text: Soak in dark rum, continue over days

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the rearranged letters sit above the days letter
rum is an old word for odd or strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to run is to continue

explanation.surface: Steep something in dark rum and keep it there for days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is an adjective meaning odd, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A soak is slang for a heavy drinker, a synonym for a drunk.

clue.text: Seeing that side is rocking

parts.note: as means since or seeing that
a wing is a side, as of a building or stage

explanation.surface: Given that one flank is swaying back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswing means swinging to and fro, which is a synonym for rocking.

clue.text: Aspiring, with honour, to eclipse posh lord

indicators.note: to eclipse means to cover, so the honour wraps around the posh lord

parts.note: an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: An ambitious person with a minor honour hopes to outshine a grand peer.
explanation.definitionFit: A would-be writer is one who aspires to be one, so the term means aspiring or hopeful.

clue.text: Criminal is angry with new lot of barristers

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook is furious with a new set of lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, the crook, but is the adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Inn is one of the four Inns of Court in London to which every English barrister belongs.

clue.text: State subsidy, part of the UK recalled, not available

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: aid is a subsidy or grant
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A government grant to a UK region is withdrawn and no longer on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory postman quickly recalled?

parts.note: off means below standard, as in an off day
Postman Pat is the children's TV postman

explanation.surface: A poor postman is being swiftly called back.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's television series about a village postman.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing something off pat means having it memorised, ready to bring to mind instantly.

clue.text: Battle possibly to contain university academic after one's number?

indicators.note: after means the name and its contents follow the numeral

parts.note: one gives the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to contain means the university and academic go inside the name

parts.note: Ben Battle is the soldier in Thomas Hood's comic poem Faithless Nelly Gray, so Ben is a possible first name for a Battle
prof is short for professor, an academic

explanation.surface: A battle that might involve a university don, after one's figure is counted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a painkilling drug, so it is a number in the sense of a thing that numbs pain.

clue.text: One's following plot that's obscure

indicators.note: following means the speaker's words come after the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed
one's, read as one is from the speaker's view, gives I'm, here IM

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are trailing a storyline that makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedim is to make dim, so it is a verb meaning to darken or obscure.

clue.text: Indian leaves preparation of report to auditors

indicators.note: to auditors means as heard by listeners, so the word for the noise is spoken

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, as of a gun

explanation.surface: An Indian quits drafting an account for the accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' seem to be accountants but are just listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhang is an Indian preparation of cannabis leaves, drunk or smoked.

clue.text: Push for one to press for payment in return

indicators.note: in return means the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
to dun is to demand payment of a debt

explanation.surface: An encouragement for someone to chase what they are owed in exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle push or prod with the elbow.

clue.text: Muck in net turned over on Spanish beach

indicators.note: on means the turned net comes after the beach

parts.note: playa is Spanish for beach

indicators.note: turned over means the catching word is read backwards

parts.note: a trap is a net for catching things

explanation.surface: Mud in a fishing net that was overturned on a beach in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To muck in is to join in and contribute, which is to play a part.

clue.text: Group of relations mostly head for France

parts.note: sexual relations, sex

indicators.note: mostly means dropping the closing letter of the French head

parts.note: tete is the French word for head

explanation.surface: Most of a family party set off to France.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a set of six musicians or things, a kind of group.

clue.text: Say "ow" after poke: blame husband!

parts.note: a dig is a poke, as in the ribs
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Someone cries out after being jabbed, then blames the husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is not an instruction to speak but means for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A digraph is a pair of letters making one sound, and the letters ow are an example of one.
